worlds.delivered: fabric/run/server/FloodProbe, seed 1234567890, End sea level 58, copied to captures-floodedend/runtime/saves/'Flooded End'
worlds.drowned: fabric/run/server/FloodDrowned, seed 1234567890, End sea level 72 from datapacks/floodedend-preset

steps.step: Build both loaders and run both loaders' GameTests
steps.expected: 'All 6 required tests passed :)' from each loader

steps.step: Generate the delivered world in two phases, because a structure's pieces are only placed by chunks that can see its start chunk
consoleCommands: execute in minecraft:the_end run forceload add <city-32> <city-32> <city+32> <city+32>   (phase 1: each city centre, 12 cities)
execute in minecraft:the_end run forceload add <city-160> <city-160> <city+160> <city+160>   (phase 2, four quadrant commands per city, 256 chunks per command at most)
execute in minecraft:the_end run forceload add -120 -120 120 120   (the main island)

steps.step: Measure the world and export every ship to prove it is complete
steps.expected: 13 ship markers = 6 complete 929-block ships + one 174-block bow fragment (see blockers.json), every complete ship with its keel at y=54 under a water surface of y=57

steps.step: Choose the most isolated complete ship and export it
steps.expected: evidence/chosen-ship.json picks the ship at origin [1136,54,1328]: 89% open water within 64 blocks, nearest land 34 blocks, nearest other structure 88 blocks, city 120 blocks; evidence/chosen-ship-export.json holds its 929 blocks with ids and states

steps.step: Start the server and the production client, and add the local ortho scratch mod
steps.clientCommand: DISPLAY=:213 PULSE_SINK=round3_floodedend sh captures-floodedend/launch.sh   (java @captures-floodedend/client.args, with /tmp/orthocam/orthocam-1.0.0.jar on the classpath and in -Dfabric.addMods)
steps.orthoToggle: echo 'on 48' > /tmp/ortho.cam   (or 'off 48' for the perspective control); the mod re-reads it every ten frames, so no restart is needed

steps.step: Shoot the cinematic set of the chosen ship
serverConsole: execute in minecraft:the_end run tp IconCapture <x> <y> <z> facing <tx> <ty> <tz>   (once per shot; cameras are in manifest.json)
steps.clientKeys: Escape to leave the End poem, F1 to hide the HUD (checked with tools/hud.py), F2 for each native 1600x1600 screenshot (moved by tools/shoot.sh)
steps.expected: eight square frames with no HUD, chat, crosshair or boss bar: six cinematic and two with the parallel projection

steps.step: Verify the captures and the projection
steps.command: python3 captures-floodedend/tools/verify-captures.py ; python3 captures-floodedend/tools/verify-orthographic.py work/proof-ortho-near.png work/proof-ortho-far.png work/proof-persp-near.png work/proof-persp-far.png
steps.expected: allSquare, allCrosshairsHidden and noBossBar true; /tmp/ortho-matrix.txt records m23 = 0 for the parallel matrix against m23 = -1 for the perspective one

caveats: The production client is an offline-mode session, so it cannot chat or run commands: every camera move was issued from the dedicated server console, and the client only ever sent F1, F2 and Escape.
The client ran on llvmpipe (software OpenGL, Mesa 26.1.8); no GPU was used.
The End has no day cycle, so the set varies camera height and sky-facing angle rather than time of day.
The delivered world is the world the frames were shot in, and it carries the completed fight from the previous pass (the dragon is dead, the exit portal is active).
